title: Rhubarb and orange compote with yoghurt

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Rhubarb, oranges, honey, almonds, Greek yoghurt and cinnamon are all plain whole foods any grandparent would have kept.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient, including forced rhubarb in March, is an everyday item at Tesco.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a saucepan, a grater and a knife, and peeling and slicing an orange is within a beginner's reach.

works.reason: 400g rhubarb with three oranges, 2 tbsp honey and 500g yoghurt makes four good bowls, and a covered 5 to 6 minute simmer suits tender March rhubarb.

honest_times.reason: Toasting the almonds, zesting, peeling and slicing the oranges and cutting the rhubarb fit within 15 minutes, and the short simmer fits the 10 minutes of cooking.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and the cinnamon appear in the steps, and nothing unlisted is used apart from water.

seasonal_feel.reason: The oranges are a full partner in the dish: zest and juice in the compote, and sliced rounds stirred through it, which suits a chilly early March morning.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant language or preaching.

hearty_healthy.reason: Fruit, Greek yoghurt and toasted almonds make a proper, filling breakfast with only modest added honey.
